passage: 'relating change to baseline values using correlation or regression is methodologically flawed due to mathematical coupling'; the relation between clinical outcomes and baseline 'were reanalysed using Oldham's method and the variance ratio test' (abstract, Europe PMC).
faulty: R-squared of the least-squares regression of the change (followup_depth - baseline_depth) on baseline_depth over the 24 defects; criterion R-squared >= 0.15.
fixed: Oldham's method as R-squared: squared correlation between the change and the mean of baseline_depth and followup_depth; criterion >= 0.15.
estimand: Faulty: variance of the change explained by the baseline reading. Fixed: variance of the change explained by the average level of the two readings.
model_family: Latent-depth model with Gaussian reading error at baseline and follow-up and an individual treatment response; Gaussian. Chosen because the source gives no model; this is the standard model behind Oldham's method; fixed for both twins.
sizes_note: Source: reanalysed 12 trials for pocket probing depth and 14 for lifetime cumulative attachment loss (abstract); the number of defects per trial is not stated. 24 defects is a realistic size for a single guided tissue regeneration trial. Size dependence: not stated.
exploited_structure: The baseline depth appears both as the predictor and inside the change, so probing error in the baseline produces an association between them.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no probing error; 0.2 corresponds to a probing error SD of about 0.9 mm against a between-defect SD of about 2 mm, a realistic figure for periodontal probing

notes: Pair case. Threshold 0.15 is below 0.2 because at n=24 the faulty R-squared must be able to reach it under noise alone; the world author sets effect sizes. Differs from B3B-05 (correlation, large n) by statistic (R-squared) and sample-size regime.
